method: Flesch Kincaid grade plus five, using a vowel-group syllable heuristic. Punctuated sentences and standalone task lines are counted as sentence units. Exact corpora and hashes retained. Quantity table fragments, headings, staff text, dates, lesson codes and the verbatim scheme outcome are excluded. Estimates guide editing; they are not learner assessments. Read-aloud and confirmed scribing routes are available.

Original invented teaching photo. Left to right: felt, woven cotton, stretch knit. It shows appearance only. The pictured knit has a finished edge; the photo does not prove stretch, fraying or curling.
These descriptions and the supplied photo are model information. Real fabrics vary. If you test an actual sample, record its real result. If no sample is available, write model information used; do not claim a test.
With an adult, use the checks below on a real sample if available. No cutting, needle or adhesive is required today. If no sample is available, use the labelled model descriptions instead.
With adult approval, hold a sample gently at two edges. Pull lightly across it, then release. Does it return to its shape?
Look at a cut edge. Does it shed threads, stay firm or curl? Do not pull threads out.
Bend the sample gently. Could it support three cards without flopping? Keep this as a prediction until the pouch is made.
Sample ___. Source actual sample / model information ___. Property ___. What I observed or read ___. What that could mean for the pouch ___. My choice and reason ___.
An actual sample result tells you about that sample. A model description supports a planning prediction. Neither proves an unmade pouch passed its final fit and handling test. Record uncertainty and a later question.
Do not force a stretch, tear an edge or pull out threads. Ask for adult handling or no-touch comparison if needed. A colour choice may matter to the user, but link at least one property to the job.

Compare the job each method does and the controls it needs. The open-top pouch needs joined sides and bottom; it needs no fastening.
Plan hand running stitch through both layers along the three seam lines. Next week the adult will show threading, a knot, small even passes about 5 mm apart and securing the end. Today you choose and explain; do not start unsupervised needle work.
Adult model: non-fraying felt with hand running stitch. Its firm shape could help hold the cards. Stitch joins the sides and bottom without an adhesive cure wait. Check the actual felt and tools before making. Your choice needs your own reason.
In your book: I choose ___ to join the sides and bottom because ___. I do / do not need a fastening because ___. Adult tool or label check still needed ___.

Design a small reusable pouch for three paper prompt cards. Each card is 60 mm wide and 80 mm high. Hold the cards upright. Join the sides and bottom; leave the top open. The pouch should be comfortable to handle, with no loose sharp parts.
Default plan: two fabric rectangles, each 100 mm wide and 120 mm high. This is 10 cm by 12 cm. Plan a seam line 10 mm inside the left, right and bottom edges. Leave the top open. These are written measurements, not a printed cutting template.
The actual finished pouch should let the cards fit without force, hold them upright and stay joined at the sides and bottom when lifted gently. Check that it is comfortable to handle and has no loose sharp parts. Today we plan these tests; we do not claim they happened.
In your book, draw and label two pieces. Show the three joined edges and the open top. Written ruler measurements govern. Any changed size or opening needs the adult’s revised design check.

An unmade design is not a completed pouch. Keep this actual decision for measuring and joining next week.

Today is choosing and planning. Use the actual classroom tool routine. An adult must approve any tool, sample test or adhesive before use.
1 Wait for adult approval before handling needles, scissors or adhesive. Use only the agreed tools and supervision.
2 Count needles out and back into a safe container. Never put pins or needles in your mouth or leave them in a product.
3 For a pause, put tools down in the agreed place. Keep fingers clear of a needle exit point. Tell the adult about a lost or damaged tool.
4 Use adhesive only after the adult checks the actual label and fabric. Follow the full cure instructions before testing. No heat, irons or solvent route is taught.
5 Today is choosing and planning. A model picture or empty-hand rehearsal does not prove textile testing or making.
Stop. Put the tool down in the agreed place. Tell the adult about a missing needle, damaged tool, unexpected material or discomfort. Restart only after the adult has resolved the concern.
With no fabric, tools, paper or printer, hear the purpose and model descriptions. Point, speak or sign a choice. Explain one property and one reason. Rehearse the plan with empty hands. An adult records exact confirmed words when a recording method is available. Mark transcription pending until it exists. Keep actual sample tests and textile making pending.
